claims.claim: wiki/getting-started.md:37-39, that on Windows the smallest supported tier is a GPU with around 8 GB of video memory, is contradicted by the planner on both available readings.
claims.evidence: The page states it at wiki/getting-started.md:37-39. Contradicted by crates/hearth-probe. Reading one, that 8 GB is where Hearth stops supporting a machine: on Windows unified_memory is false (machine.rs:82), so base is stt 805306368 plus headroom 1073741824 = 1879048192 (plan.rs:110-113 with dictionary.yaml:84 and 89), and Windows is in cpp_platforms (dictionary.yaml:102) so the voice holds 966367641 (dictionary.yaml:113). The smallest plan the dictionary can produce is tier 0's Q3_K_M at 2536786016 (dictionary.yaml:176) plus a MIN_CTX floor of 12288 times 4096 = 50331648 (plan.rs:14 and 302), so 2587117664 of budget. PlanError::TooSmall at plan.rs:151-157 fires only when even sequential_budget misses that, which is a pool below 4466165856 bytes: about 4.5 GB decimal, and 4.16 GB in the units crates/hearth-probe/src/lib.rs:26-34 actually prints. The Windows floor is therefore roughly 4.5 GB of VRAM, not 8 GB. Reading two, that an 8 GB card lands on the smallest tier: an 8 GB card has a pool of 8589934592 and a coexist_budget of 5744518759, which clears tier 1 Gemma 4 E4B at 4977171584 plus its 20480 times 4096 = 83886080 floor (dictionary.yaml:185 and 189), so the coexist arm at plan.rs:128-136 returns tier 1, labelled Small, one tier above the smallest. The budget arithmetic and the take-turns band were first derived in tasks/docs/artifacts/T2.research.json; every constant and branch condition cited here was re-read from source this session.

notes:
The dispatch's central direction is overturned by evidence, which the dispatch itself invited. A genuine distribution point exists: https://github.com/XXJones21/Hearth/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha carries Hearth_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe, Hearth_0.1.0_x64_en-US.msi, Hearth_0.1.0_aarch64.dmg, Hearth_0.1.0_android.apk and SHA256SUMS.txt, published 2026-08-22T03:20:11Z and flagged prerelease. Building from the repository is therefore not the only path a reader has, and an author told that it is would understate what a reader can do. The orchestrator's grep was sound and its conclusion followed from it; what a grep of wiki/ could not see is that the corpus never links a thing that already exists. Three independent corroborations rule out a bad fetch: the live asset names are exactly the Hearth_<v> names wiki/releasing.md:39-41 predicts, the publication date matches wiki/releasing.md:208 to the day, and the release notes end with the exact sentence wiki/releasing.md:203-204 quotes as 0.1.0's closing line. git remote -v confirms XXJones21/Hearth is this worktree's origin. What remains true from the corrected premise is the shape of the fix: the honest content is a statement plus a link, not an invented URL, and it now has a verified URL to point at.

Sized S rather than the M the tracker carried, and the reason is that the research this task was waiting on is now finished. M requires several pages or one net-new page, and neither holds: exactly one file changes, wiki/getting-started.md, which is 83 lines rather than the 84 the dispatch stated. Two of its four sections drop outright, verified as pure duplication by locating all seven links at lines 67-76 already present in wiki/_index.md. type: how-to becomes type: concept on line 4, which scripts/lint_wiki.py:48-50 accepts. ## What you need needs one contradicted sentence replaced, and choosing the replacement number is an editorial call recorded in open_questions rather than a research gap. The new statement of how a reader obtains Hearth has a verified URL, verified artifact names and sizes, verified platform coverage and a verified unsigned-dmg caveat, so nothing is left to discover. Retyping breaks no inbound link because the path does not move.

Type and Mode agree. Type is Fix, Mode is affected, and the tracker's row at line 29 calls it Restructure, which is a narrower label for the same work and does not change the survey shape.

On tooling. Bash was available in this session, contrary to the caller's warning, and I used it only for grep, find, sed, cat, wc, git remote -v, and the repository's own read-only scripts. python scripts/lint_wiki.py ran and reports 28 pages checked, 0 errors, 198 warnings, with the only finding on this page being wiki/getting-started.md:36: [long-paragraph] 80 words. I did not run scripts/doc_graph.py, which is a graph-mode instrument and was not needed to survey a single page. WebFetch was used three times, all against github.com or api.github.com, because whether a public release exists is a question about a hosted service rather than about the source tree and cannot be settled by reading the repository. One heredoc write of this artifact failed on embedded backticks, so the file was written with the Write tool instead; no other file was created or modified.

On borrowed evidence. Two claims lean on earlier runs and say so inline. The Windows budget arithmetic and the take-turns band come from tasks/docs/artifacts/T2.research.json; the unified-memory arithmetic and the 8 GB Mac coexistence come from tasks/docs/artifacts/T1.research.json. In both cases I re-read the underlying constants from crates/hearth-probe/dictionary.yaml, crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs, crates/hearth-probe/src/machine.rs and crates/hearth-probe/tests/plan_fixtures.rs this session and cite those lines directly. I executed no Rust and ran no probe; the arithmetic is derived from constants I read, as it was in T1 and T2.

One correction to the record, reported and not acted on: tasks/docs/tracker.md cites wiki/installing.md:24 for You have the Hearth installer at both :909 and :1097. The sentence is at line 27. The reasoning built on it is unaffected.
